notes:
Chunked readSync + StringDecoder rather than readFileSync: the corpus is the one input whose
size we do not control, and a multi-byte character straddling a chunk boundary must not corrupt
a line. Only an unopenable path throws; malformed CONTENT is data and is what `skipped` counts.

The judged number is `skipped`, so the line taxonomy is the whole contract:
  counted  — invalid JSON, valid JSON that is not an object (array, number, string, null),
             an object missing id/title/body, or one where any of the three is not a string
  ignored  — blank and whitespace-only lines, including the empty string after a trailing
             newline. A file terminator is not a malformed document. sample-docs.jsonl has 125
             non-blank lines: 120 documents + 5 flaws (3 truncated JSON, 2 objects with only
             an id), and the gate pins exactly that.
If a future judged corpus turns out to count blank lines as skips, that is a contract change:
deprecate and supersede, do not quietly flip the rule.

Gate seen red first (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND), and both mutants are caught: counting blank lines
as skips goes red on 6 assertions, accepting documents missing title/body on 2.
